\label{cor:SV}
Let $p>1$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded open set. Then
\[
T_p(\Omega)\leq T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)\leq T_p(\Omega^\star)=\frac{(p-1)\,\omega_n^{-\frac{p}{n(p-1)}}}{n^{\frac{1}{p-1}}\,\big(n(p-1)+p\big)}\,|\Omega|^{\frac{n(p-1)+p}{n(p-1)}},
\]
where $\omega_n=|B^n|$. Equality holds in the second inequality if and only if $\Omega$ is an ellipsoid, up to a set of zero Sobolev $p$-capacity.

label: thm:potential
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:potential}
Let $1<p<n$ and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a compact set with $|K|>0$. There exists $u\in D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\tilde u\geq1$ quasi-everywhere on $K$ and $\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p=\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)$. Every such minimizer satisfies $0\leq u\leq1$ and $\tilde u=1$ quasi-everywhere on $K$, and it is the unique capacitary potential of $K$ for the anisotropic energy $v\mapsto\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}H_u(\nabla v)^p\,dx$. Moreover, $\Delta^{\mathcal{A}}_pu=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K$, and $\mu_K=\Delta^{\mathcal{A}}_pu$ is a nonnegative Radon measure supported on $\partial K$ with $\mu_K(\mathbb{R}^n)=\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)$.

label: thm:isocap
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:isocap}
Let $1<p<n$ and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a compact set with $|K|>0$. Then
\[
\operatorname{cap}_p(K)\geq\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)\geq\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star),
\]
and equality holds in the second inequality  if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid up to a set of zero Sobolev $p$-capacity, that is, $E\subseteq K$ and $C_p(K\setminus E)=0$ for some closed ellipsoid $E$.

label: thm:stab
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:stab}
Let $\beta=2$ if $p=2$ and $\beta=1680(n+p)$ if $p\neq2$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Let $p>1$ and $1\leq q<p^*$. There is $c=c(n,p,q)>0$ such that, for every bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$,
\[
\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\big(1+c\,\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(\Omega)^{\beta}\big)\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star).
\]
In particular, $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)\leq\big(1+c\,\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(\Omega)^{\beta}\big)^{-1/(p-1)}T_p(\Omega^\star)$ when $q=1$.
\item Let $1<p<n$. There is $c=c(n,p)>0$ such that, for every compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $|K|>0$,
\[
\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)\geq\big(1+c\,\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(K)^{\beta}\big)\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star).
\]

\item Let $p>1$ and $1<q<p^*$. For every $\eta>0$ there is $\varepsilon=\varepsilon(n,p,q,\eta)>0$ with the following property. If $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a bounded open convex set such that
\[
T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)\leq(1+\varepsilon)\,T_p(B^n)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda_{p,q}(B^n),
\]
then there is an open ellipsoid $E$, with center $z$, such that $E\subseteq\Omega\subseteq z+e^{\eta}(E-z)$; in particular, $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(\Omega)\leq e^{n\eta}-1$.
\end{enumerate}

label: thm:DPMM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:DPMM}
There exists $c_{\mathrm{cap}}=c_{\mathrm{cap}}(n,p)>0$ such that
\[
\operatorname{cap}_p(K)\geq\big(1+c_{\mathrm{cap}}\,\mathcal{F}(K)^2\big)\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star)
\]
for every compact set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $|K|>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For open sets of finite measure this is \cite[Theorem 1.4]{Mukoseeva2023} (see \cite{DPMM2021} for $p=2$), written in scale-invariant form by means of the scaling of the capacity. Let $K$ be compact with $|K|>0$ and apply it to the open neighborhoods $K_t$. As $t\to0$, $\operatorname{cap}_p(K_t)\to\operatorname{cap}_p(K)$, $|K_t|\to|K|$ and $\operatorname{cap}_p(K_t^\star)\to\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star)$, where $K_t^\star$ is the ball of volume $|K_t|$. If $B_t$ is a ball with $|B_t|=|K_t|$ and $|K_t\triangle B_t|\leq(\mathcal{F}(K_t)+t)|K_t|$, and $B'_t$ is the concentric ball with $|B'_t|=|K|$, then $|K\triangle B'_t|\leq(\mathcal{F}(K_t)+t)|K_t|+2(|K_t|-|K|)$, so that $\mathcal{F}(K)\leq\liminf_{t\to0}\mathcal{F}(K_t)$. The inequality for $K$ follows by letting $t\to0$.

label: prop:energy
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:energy}
Let $p>1$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded open set, and let $f\in W^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, or $f\in D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ if $1<p<n$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$, $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $t>0$, one has $\mathcal{E}_p(|f|)=\mathcal{E}_p(f\circ A)=\mathcal{E}_p(f(\cdot+x_0))=\mathcal{E}_p(f)$ and $\mathcal{E}_p(f(\cdot/t))=t^{(n-p)/p}\,\mathcal{E}_p(f)$.
\item There are $t_p>0$, depending only on $p$, and $C=C(n,p,\Omega)>0$ such that, for every $g\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ and $\xi\in S^{n-1}$,
\[
\|\nabla_\xi g\|_p\geq t_p\,w(\Omega,\xi)^{-1}\|g\|_p\qquad\text{and}\qquad\mathcal{E}_p(g)\geq C\,\|g\|_p^{\frac{n-1}{n}}\|\nabla g\|_p^{\frac1n},
\]
where $w(\Omega,\xi)$ is the width of $\Omega$ in the direction $\xi$.
\item $\mathcal{E}_p$ is continuous for the norm topology on $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)\setminus\{0\}$ and, if $1<p<n$, on $D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)\setminus\{0\}$, and it is sequentially weakly lower semicontinuous on $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$.
\item If $1<p<n$, then $S_{n,p}\|f\|_{p^*}\leq\mathcal{E}_p(f)$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:GammaPi} and polar coordinates, $h(\Gamma_pL,\zeta)^p=\frac{1}{n\,a_{n,p}\,|L|}\int_{S^{n-1}}\rho_L(\xi)^{n+p}|\langle\zeta,\xi\rangle|^p\,d\xi$ for $\zeta\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Hence, by Fubini's theorem, $|L|=\omega_n$ and \eqref{eq:dualmixed},
\begin{align}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}h(\Gamma_pL,\nabla f)^p\,dx&=\frac{1}{n\omega_n a_{n,p}}\int_{S^{n-1}}\rho_L(\xi)^{n+p}\,\|\nabla_\xi f\|_p^p\,d\xi\\
    &= \frac{1}{\omega_n a_{n,p}}\widetilde{V}_{-p}(L,\Pi^*_pf)\\
    &\geq a_{n,p}^{-1}\, \omega_n^{\frac{p}{n}}|\Pi^*_pf|^{-\frac{p}{n}} = \mathcal{E}_p(f)^p.
\end{align}
Equality holds if and only if $L$ and $\Pi_p^* f$ are dilates, that is, if and only if $L = L_f$.

label: lem:admissible
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:admissible}
Let $p>1$ and let $L$ be a star body. Then the norm $h(\Gamma_pL,\cdot)$ is strictly convex and of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By \eqref{eq:GammaPi}, $h(\Gamma_pL,x)$ is a constant multiple of the $L^p(L)$ norm of the linear function $y\mapsto\langle x,y\rangle$. If $h(\Gamma_pL,x+x')=h(\Gamma_pL,x)+h(\Gamma_pL,x')$ with $x,x'\neq0$, the equality case of Minkowski's inequality, $1<p<\infty$, shows that $\langle x,\cdot\rangle$ and $\langle x',\cdot\rangle$ are positively proportional on $L$, which has non-empty interior; hence $x'$ is a positive multiple of $x$, and $(\Gamma_pL)^\circ$ is strictly convex. Differentiation under the integral sign, legitimate because $p>1$ and $L$ is bounded, shows that $h(\Gamma_pL,\cdot)^p$ is of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, and hence $h(\Gamma_pL,\cdot)$ is of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$. Since $\langle\nabla h(\Gamma_pL,x),x\rangle=h(\Gamma_pL,x)=1$ on $\partial(\Gamma_pL)^\circ$, the gradient does not vanish there, and $(\Gamma_pL)^\circ$ has $C^1$ boundary.

label: lem:Wulff
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Wulff}
Let $Q$ be an origin-symmetric convex body.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For $1\leq q<p^*$,
\[
\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q)=\Big(\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\Big)^{1-\frac pq}\Lambda_{p,q}(B^n)\qquad\text{and}\qquad T^{Q}_p(Q)=\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\,T_p(B^n).
\]
Consequently, for $1<q<p^*$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Wulff}
T^{Q}_p(Q)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q)=\Big(\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\Big)^{\theta}\kappa,\qquad\theta=\frac{p^2(q-1)}{q\,(n(p-1)+p)}>0,
\end{equation}
where $\kappa=T_p(B^n)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda_{p,q}(B^n)$.
\item If $1<p<n$ and $K$ is compact, then $\operatorname{cap}^{Q}_p(K)\geq(|Q|/\omega_n)^{p/n}\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star)$.
\item If $Q=AB^n$ with $A\in\mathrm{GL}(n)$ and $\det A>0$, then, for every open set $\Omega$ of finite measure, every $1\leq q<p^*$ and, if $1<p<n$, every compact set $K$,
\[
\begin{gathered}
\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)=(\det A)^{1-\frac pq}\,\Lambda_{p,q}(A^{-1}\Omega),\qquad T^{Q}_p(\Omega)=(\det A)\,T_p(A^{-1}\Omega),\\
\operatorname{cap}^{Q}_p(K)=(\det A)\operatorname{cap}_p(A^{-1}K).
\end{gathered}
\]
In particular, if $A=tA_0$ with $t>0$ and $A_0\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$, then $\operatorname{cap}^{Q}_p(K)=t^p\operatorname{cap}_p(A_0^{-1}K)$.
\item If $\Omega$ is a bounded open set and $1\leq q<p^*$, then
\[
\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\Big(\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\Big)^{\frac pn}\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)\qquad\text{and}\qquad T^{Q}_p(\Omega)\leq\Big(\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\Big)^{-\frac{p}{n(p-1)}}T_p(\Omega^\star).
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) By the convex symmetrization of Alvino, Ferone, Lions and Trombetti \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AFLT1997}, for every nonnegative $v\in W^{1,p}_0(Q)$ the function equimeasurable with $v$ whose superlevel sets are dilates of $Q$ belongs to $W^{1,p}_0(Q)$ and has smaller or equal anisotropic energy $\int h_Q(\nabla\cdot)^p\,dx$. Hence the infimum defining $\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q)$ may be restricted to functions of the form $v(x)=g(\|x\|_Q)$, where $g$ is locally absolutely continuous on $(0,1]$ and $g(1)=0$. For such $v$, $h_Q(\nabla v(x))=|g'(\|x\|_Q)|$ for a.e. $x$, because $h_Q(\nabla\|x\|_Q)=1$ wherever the gauge is differentiable. Since $|\{\|x\|_Q<t\}|=t^n|Q|$, the coarea formula gives
\[
\int_Qh_Q(\nabla v)^p\,dx=n|Q|\int_0^1|g'(t)|^pt^{n-1}\,dt,\qquad\int_Q|v|^q\,dx=n|Q|\int_0^1|g(t)|^qt^{n-1}\,dt.
\]
The same identities hold for the Euclidean energy of $g(|x|)$ on $B^n$, with $|Q|$ replaced by $\omega_n$. Consequently $\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q)=(n|Q|)^{1-p/q}m$ and $\Lambda_{p,q}(B^n)=(n\omega_n)^{1-p/q}m$, where $m$ is the infimum of
\[
\frac{\int_0^1|g'(t)|^p\,t^{n-1}\,dt}{\big(\int_0^1|g(t)|^q\,t^{n-1}\,dt\big)^{p/q}}
\]
over all functions $g\not\equiv0$ that are locally absolutely continuous on $(0,1]$ with $g(1)=0$.
The case $q=1$ gives the second one (see also \cite[Lemma 6.2]{Brasco2014}). Finally, \eqref{eq:Wulff} follows from the identity $(p-1)\sigma+1-\frac pq=\theta$.

(ii) Let $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\varphi\geq1$ on $K$; replacing $\varphi$ by $\min\{\max\{\varphi,0\},1\}$, which does not increase the anisotropic energy, we may assume that $\varphi$ is Lipschitz, compactly supported and takes values in $[0,1]$. As above, its convex symmetrization $\varphi^{Q}$ satisfies $\int h_Q(\nabla\varphi^{Q})^p\leq\int h_Q(\nabla\varphi)^p$ by \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AFLT1997}. Moreover, $\varphi^{Q}\geq1$ on the dilate $sQ$ of $Q$ with $|sQ|=|K|$, because $|\{\varphi\geq1\}|\geq|K|$. As in (i), for a function $v(x)=g(\|x\|_Q)$ the coarea formula gives
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}h_Q(\nabla v)^p\,dx=\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|\nabla\big(g(|x|)\big)\big|^p\,dx.
\]
Writing $\varphi^{Q}(x)=g(\|x\|_Q)$, the function $g(|x|)$ is admissible for $\overline{B}_s$, and therefore $\int h_Q(\nabla\varphi)^p\geq(|Q|/\omega_n)\operatorname{cap}_p(\overline{B}_s)$. Since $|\overline{B}_s|=\omega_n|K|/|Q|$, the scaling of the capacity gives
\[
\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\operatorname{cap}_p(\overline{B}_s)=\Big(\frac{|Q|}{\omega_n}\Big)^{p/n}\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star),
\]
and (ii) follows by taking the infimum over $\varphi$.

(iii) We have $h_Q(\zeta)=|A^{\mathrm{T}}\zeta|$. If $v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ and $w(y)=v(Ay)$, then $w\in W^{1,p}_0(A^{-1}\Omega)$ and $\nabla w(y)=A^{\mathrm{T}}\nabla v(Ay)$, and the substitution $x=Ay$ gives $\int_\Omega h_Q(\nabla v)^p\,dx=(\det A)\int|\nabla w|^p\,dy$ and $\int_\Omega|v|^q\,dx=(\det A)\int|w|^q\,dy$, which proves the first two identities. In the same way, $u\in\mathcal{W}(K)$ if and only if $u\circ A\in\mathcal{W}(A^{-1}K)$, which proves the third one. If $A=tA_0$, then $\det A=t^n$ and $\operatorname{cap}_p(A^{-1}K)=t^{p-n}\operatorname{cap}_p(A_0^{-1}K)$ by the scaling of the capacity.

(iv) Since $h_Q$ is even, the infimum defining $\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)$ may be taken over nonnegative functions. Let $s>0$ satisfy $|sQ|=|\Omega|$, and $v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ be a non-negative function. The convex symmetrization of $v$ belongs to $W^{1,p}_0(sQ)$, has the same $L^q$ norm and has smaller or equal anisotropic energy by \cite[Theorem 3.1]{AFLT1997}. Hence $\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(sQ)=s^{\,n-p-np/q}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q)$. If $\rho$ is the radius of $\Omega^\star$, then $s^n|Q|=\rho^n\omega_n$, and by (i) and the scaling $\Lambda_{p,q}(\rho B^n)=\rho^{\,n-p-np/q}\,\Lambda_{p,q}(B^n)$ the right-hand side equals $(|Q|/\omega_n)^{p/n}\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)$. The case $q=1$ gives the inequality for $T^{Q}_p$.

label: prop:p2
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:p2}
Let $f\in W^{1,2}_0(\Omega)\setminus\{0\}$ for a bounded open set $\Omega$, or $f\in D^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^n)\setminus\{0\}$ with $n\geq3$, and let $Q_f=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\nabla f\otimes\nabla f\,dx$. Then
\[
\mathcal{E}_2(f)^2=n\det(Q_f)^{1/n}=\min_{A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)}\|\nabla(f\circ A)\|_2^2,
\]
and the minimum is attained exactly when $AA^{\mathrm{T}}=\det(Q_f)^{1/n}Q_f^{-1}$. Consequently, for every bounded open set $\Omega$ and every $1\leq q<2^*$,
\[
\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{2,q}(\Omega)=\min_{A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)}\Lambda_{2,q}(A\Omega),\qquad T^{\mathcal{A}}_2(\Omega)=\max_{A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)}T_2(A\Omega),
\]
and, if $n\geq3$, $\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_2(K)=\inf_{A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)}\operatorname{cap}_2(AK)$ for every compact set $K$, with the infimum attained if $|K|>0$.

title: Proof
body_md:

abla_\xi f$ vanishes outside $\Omega$, H"older's inequality gives $\|

label: prop:attain
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:attain}
Let $p>1$, $1\leq q<p^*$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded open set. Then $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)>0$, and it is attained by a nonnegative function.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $(v_k)\subset W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ be a minimizing sequence with $\|v_k\|_q=1$; replacing $v_k$ by $|v_k|$ we may assume $v_k\geq0$. We claim that $\inf_k\|v_k\|_p>0$. If $q\leq p$, this follows from H\"older's inequality, $1=\|v_k\|_q\leq|\Omega|^{\frac1q-\frac1p}\|v_k\|_p$. If $q>p$, choose $s\in(q,\infty)$ as follows: $s=p^*$ if $p<n$, and $s=r^*=nr/(n-r)$ for some $r\in(1,n)$ with $r^*>q$ if $p\geq n$. By the affine Sobolev inequality \eqref{eq:affineSobolev} at the exponent $p$, respectively at the exponent $r$ combined with Lemma \ref{lem:lower}, the sequence $(v_k)$ is bounded in $L^s$. Writing $\frac1q=\frac\lambda p+\frac{1-\lambda}{s}$ with $\lambda\in(0,1)$, the interpolation inequality $1=\|v_k\|_q\leq\|v_k\|_p^\lambda\|v_k\|_s^{1-\lambda}$ proves the claim. Proposition \ref{prop:energy}(ii) now shows that $(v_k)$ is bounded in $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$. By the Rellich--Kondrachov theorem, a subsequence converges weakly in $W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$ and strongly in $L^q(\Omega)$ to a function $u\geq0$ with $\|u\|_q=1$, and by Proposition \ref{prop:energy}(iii), $\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p\leq\liminf_k\mathcal{E}_p(v_k)^p=\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$. Hence $u$ is a minimizer, and $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p>0$ by Proposition \ref{prop:energy}(ii).

label: lem:slicing
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:slicing}
Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a compact set with $|K|>0$, and let $f\in D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ satisfy $f=1$ a.e. on $K$ and $\|f\|_{p^*}\leq m$. Then, for every $\xi\in S^{n-1}$,
\[
\|\nabla_\xi f\|_p^p\geq c_K=2^{-p}\big(2^{p^*}m^{p^*}\big)^{1-p}\Big(\frac{|K|}{\operatorname{diam}K}\Big)^p.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $\xi\in S^{n-1}$, write $x=x'+\tau\xi$ with $x'\in\xi^\perp$, and let $g_{x'}(\tau)=f(x'+\tau\xi)$. For a.e. $x'$, the function $g_{x'}$ is locally absolutely continuous with $g_{x'}'(\tau)=\nabla_\xi f(x'+\tau\xi)$ for a.e. $\tau$, and $g_{x'}=1$ a.e. on $\{\tau:x'+\tau\xi\in K\}$; by Fubini's theorem, $\|\nabla_\xi f\|_p^p=\int_{\xi^\perp}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|g_{x'}'|^p\,d\tau\,dx'$. Let $\ell_K(x')$ and $\ell(x')$ be the lengths of $\{\tau:x'+\tau\xi\in K\}$ and of $\{\tau:g_{x'}(\tau)\geq\frac12\}$, and let $G=\{x'\in\xi^\perp:\ell_K(x')>0\}$. Since $\ell_K\leq\operatorname{diam}K$, we have $|K|=\int_G\ell_K\,dx'\leq|G|\operatorname{diam}K$, where $|G|$ is the $(n-1)$-dimensional measure of $G$; moreover $\int_{\xi^\perp}\ell\,dx'=|\{f\geq\frac12\}|\leq2^{p^*}m^{p^*}$.

Fix $x'\in G$ for which $g=g_{x'}$ has the properties above and $\ell(x')<\infty$. Since $g=1$ a.e. on $\{\tau:x'+\tau\xi\in K\}$, we have $\ell(x')\geq\ell_K(x')>0$, and, $g$ being continuous, $g(\tau_0)=1$ for some $\tau_0$. As $\{g\geq\frac12\}$ has length $\ell(x')$, the closed interval $[\tau_0,\tau_0+\ell(x')]$ contains a point $\tau_1$ with $g(\tau_1)\leq\frac12$. By H\"older's inequality,
\[
\tfrac12\leq g(\tau_0)-g(\tau_1)\leq\ell(x')^{1-\frac1p}\Big(\int_{\mathbb{R}}|g'|^p\,d\tau\Big)^{\frac1p},
\]
and therefore $\int_{\mathbb{R}}|g'|^p\,d\tau\geq2^{-p}\ell(x')^{1-p}$. Integrating over $G$ and applying Jensen's inequality to the convex function $t\mapsto t^{1-p}$, we obtain
\[
\|\nabla_\xi f\|_p^p\geq2^{-p}\int_G\ell^{1-p}\,dx'\geq2^{-p}|G|^p\Big(\int_G\ell\,dx'\Big)^{1-p}\geq2^{-p}\Big(\frac{|K|}{\operatorname{diam}K}\Big)^p\big(2^{p^*}m^{p^*}\big)^{1-p}.
\qedhere
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(f_j)\subset\mathcal{W}(K)$ be a minimizing sequence for $\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)$. Truncation does not increase the directional energies, so we may assume $0\leq f_j\leq1$, hence $f_j=1$ a.e. on $K$; and, for $j$ large, Proposition \ref{prop:energy}(iv) gives $\|f_j\|_{p^*}\leq m=S_{n,p}^{-1}(\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)+1)^{1/p}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:slicing}, $\|\nabla_\xi f_j\|_p\geq c_K^{1/p}$ for all $\xi$, that is, $\Pi^*_pf_j\subseteq RB^n$ with $R=c_K^{-1/p}$. On the other hand, since $\mathcal{E}_p(f_j)^p\leq\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)+1$ for $j$ large,
\[
|\Pi^*_pf_j|=\frac1n\Big(\frac{c_{n,p}}{\mathcal{E}_p(f_j)}\Big)^n\geq v_0=\frac{c_{n,p}^{\,n}}{n}\big(\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)+1\big)^{-n/p}>0.
\]
Hence, $\Pi^*_pf_j$ is an origin-symmetric convex body contained in $RB^n$ with volume at least $v_0$ and, therefore, it contains $\rho_0B^n$, where $\rho_0=v_0/(2\omega_{n-1}R^{n-1})$; indeed, if $r$ is the distance from the origin to its boundary, then, by symmetry, it lies in a slab of width $2r$, whose intersection with $RB^n$ has volume at most $2r\,\omega_{n-1}R^{n-1}$. As a consequence, 
\[
c_K^{1/p}\leq\|\nabla_\xi f_j\|_p\leq\rho_0^{-1}\qquad\text{for all }\xi\in S^{n-1}\text{ and all large }j,
\]
and, by \eqref{eq:average}, $(f_j)$ is bounded in $D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. A subsequence converges weakly to a function $u$, which belongs to $\mathcal{W}(K)$ because this class is weakly closed. For every $\xi$, $\|\nabla_\xi u\|_p\leq\liminf_j\|\nabla_\xi f_j\|_p$, that is, $\rho_{\Pi^*_pu}\geq\limsup_j\rho_{\Pi^*_pf_j}$ pointwise on $S^{n-1}$. These radial functions are bounded by $R$, so the reverse Fatou lemma gives $|\Pi^*_pu|\geq\limsup_j|\Pi^*_pf_j|$, that is, $\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p\leq\liminf_j\mathcal{E}_p(f_j)^p=\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)$. Thus $u$ is a minimizer.

Now let $u$ be any minimizer. Its truncation $v=\min\{\max\{u,0\},1\}$ belongs to $\mathcal{W}(K)$ and satisfies $\|\nabla_\xi v\|_p\leq\|\nabla_\xi u\|_p$ for every $\xi$. Since $\mathcal{E}_p(v)\geq\mathcal{E}_p(u)$ and both functions of $\xi$ are continuous, equality holds for every $\xi$, so that $\nabla u=0$ a.e. on $\{u<0\}\cup\{u>1\}$ and hence $u=v$. Thus $0\leq u\leq1$ and $\tilde u=1$ q.e. on $K$; in particular $\nabla u=0$ a.e. on $K$.

Let $H=H_u$. For every $w\in\mathcal{W}(K)$, Lemma \ref{lem:frozen} gives
\[
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}H(\nabla w)^p\,dx\geq\mathcal{E}_p(w)^p\geq\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)=\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}H(\nabla u)^p\,dx,
\]
so $u$ minimizes the anisotropic energy of $H$ on $\mathcal{W}(K)$. Since $H$ is a strictly convex norm of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$ (Lemma \ref{lem:admissible}) and $p>1$, the function $H^p$ is strictly convex, and $u$ is the only minimizer. The functional $w\mapsto\int H(\nabla w)^p\,dx$ is of class $C^1$ on $D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with derivative at $u$ equal to $p\,\mu$, where
\[
\langle\mu,\varphi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}H(\nabla u)^{p-1}\langle\nabla H(\nabla u),\nabla\varphi\rangle\,dx,
\]
and $\mu=\Delta^{\mathcal{A}}_pu$ in the sense of distributions, by Lemma \ref{lem:frozen}. If $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\varphi\geq0$, then $u+t\varphi\in\mathcal{W}(K)$ for $t>0$, so $\langle\mu,\varphi\rangle\geq0$; thus $\mu$ is a nonnegative distribution, that is, a nonnegative Radon measure. If $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K)$, then $u+t\varphi\in\mathcal{W}(K)$ for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$, so $\langle\mu,\varphi\rangle=0$; and if $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\operatorname{int}K)$, then $\langle\mu,\varphi\rangle=0$ because $\nabla u=0$ a.e. on $K$. Hence $\Delta^{\mathcal{A}}_pu=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K$ and $\mu$ is supported on $\partial K$.

Finally, let $\psi\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be equal to $1$ on a neighborhood of $K$, so that $\mu(\mathbb{R}^n)=\langle\mu,\psi\rangle$. The function $w=\psi-u$ satisfies $\tilde w=0$ q.e. on $K$, so it is a limit in $D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of functions in $C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K)$ (Section \ref{sec:functions}), on which $\mu$ vanishes; as $\mu$ is continuous on $D^{1,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $\langle\mu,w\rangle=0$. Therefore, by Euler's identity $\langle\nabla H(\zeta),\zeta\rangle=H(\zeta)$,
\[
\mu(\mathbb{R}^n)=\langle\mu,u\rangle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}H(\nabla u)^p\,dx=\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K).
\qedhere
\]

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:filling}
Let $\hat K$ be the union of $K$ with the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K$. Then $\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)=\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\hat K)$. Indeed, if $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\varphi\geq1$ on $K$, the function equal to $\min\{\max\{\varphi,0\},1\}$ on the unbounded component of $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus K$ and to $1$ on $\hat K$ is Lipschitz, has compact support and directional energies not larger than those of $\varphi$, and a mollification of a slightly larger multiple of it is admissible for $\hat K$. Applied to a sequence approximating a minimizer for $K$, the same construction shows that every such minimizer equals $1$ a.e. on $\hat K$. Consequently, Theorem \ref{thm:potential} holds whenever $|\hat K|>0$, for instance when $K$ is the boundary of a bounded open set. On the other hand, the affine capacity of a compact set with $|\hat K|=0$ may vanish, as for subsets of hyperplanes \cite[Theorem 2.3(i)]{XiaoZhang2016}, and we do not know whether it is attained when it is positive.

label: lem:radial
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:radial}
Let $p>1$, $1\leq q<p^*$ and $R>0$, and let $w\in W^{1,p}_0(B_R)$ be a nonnegative, radially symmetric and radially nonincreasing function with $\|w\|_q=1$ and $\|\nabla w\|_p^p=\Lambda_{p,q}(B_R)$. Write $w(x)=\varphi(|x|)$, where $\varphi$ is nonincreasing and locally absolutely continuous on $(0,R)$. Then $\varphi>0$ on $(0,R)$ and $\varphi'<0$ a.e. in $(0,R)$. In particular, $\{w>0\}=B_R$ up to a null set, and
\[
\big|\{x\in B_R:\ \nabla w(x)=0,\ 0<w(x)<\operatorname{ess\,sup}w\}\big|=0.
\]
head: environment

label: eq:EL
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Lambda=\Lambda_{p,q}(B_R)$. We first show that, with the convention $w^0=1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:EL}
\int_{B_R}|\nabla w|^{p-2}\langle\nabla w,\nabla\psi\rangle\,dx=\Lambda\int_{B_R}w^{q-1}\psi\,dx\qquad\text{for every }\psi\in W^{1,p}_0(B_R).
\end{equation}
If $q>1$, the function $t\mapsto\|\nabla(w+t\psi)\|_p^p-\Lambda\|w+t\psi\|_q^p$ is nonnegative, vanishes at $t=0$ and is differentiable there, so its derivative at $t=0$ vanishes, which is \eqref{eq:EL}. If $q=1$, then $\int w=1$, and for $|t|$ small the function $g(t)=\|\nabla(w+t\psi)\|_p^p-\Lambda\big(\int(w+t\psi)\,dx\big)^p$ satisfies $g(t)\geq\|\nabla(w+t\psi)\|_p^p-\Lambda\|w+t\psi\|_1^p\geq0=g(0)$; hence $g'(0)=0$, which is again \eqref{eq:EL}.

Now take $\psi(x)=\eta(|x|)$ with $\eta\in C^\infty([0,R])$ constant near $0$ and vanishing near $R$. In polar coordinates, \eqref{eq:EL} becomes
\begin{equation}\label{eq:radialEL}
\int_0^RG\,\eta'\,dr=\int_0^Rh\,\eta\,dr,\qquad G(r)=r^{n-1}|\varphi'(r)|^{p-2}\varphi'(r),\quad h(r)=\Lambda\,r^{n-1}\varphi(r)^{q-1}.
\end{equation}
By H\"older's inequality, $G$ and $h$ belong to $L^1(0,R)$. Choosing $\eta\in C^\infty_c(0,R)$ in \eqref{eq:radialEL} shows that $G'=-h$ in the sense of distributions on $(0,R)$; hence $G$ coincides a.e. with an absolutely continuous function, still denoted by $G$, which extends continuously to $[0,R]$. Integrating by parts in \eqref{eq:radialEL} with $\eta(0)=1$ yields $G(0)=0$, and therefore
\[
G(r)=-\Lambda\int_0^rs^{n-1}\varphi(s)^{q-1}\,ds\qquad\text{for every }r\in(0,R).
\]
Since $w\neq0$ and $\varphi$ is nonincreasing, $\varphi>0$ near $0$, so the integral is positive for every $r\in(0,R)$; thus $G<0$ on $(0,R)$, that is, $\varphi'<0$ a.e. in $(0,R)$. If $\varphi(r_1)=0$ for some $r_1<R$, then $\varphi$ vanishes on $[r_1,R)$ and $\varphi'=0$ there, a contradiction. Hence $\varphi>0$ on $(0,R)$. The last assertion follows because $|\nabla w(x)|=|\varphi'(|x|)|$ for a.e. $x$.

label: eq:isochain
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)\setminus\{0\}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:frozen}, Lemma \ref{lem:Wulff}(iv) with $Q=\Gamma_pL_v$, and the $L_p$ Busemann--Petty centroid inequality \eqref{eq:BP}, since $|L_v|=\omega_n$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:isochain}
\mathcal{E}_p(v)^p=\int_\Omega H_v(\nabla v)^p\,dx\geq\Lambda^{\Gamma_pL_v}_{p,q}(\Omega)\,\|v\|_q^p\geq\Big(\frac{|\Gamma_pL_v|}{|L_v|}\Big)^{\frac pn}\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)\,\|v\|_q^p\geq\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)\,\|v\|_q^p.
\end{equation}
Taking the infimum over $v$ proves \eqref{eq:iso}.

Suppose that $\Omega\subseteq E$ and $C_p(E\setminus\Omega)=0$ for an open ellipsoid $E$. By Section \ref{sec:functions}, $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(E)$, and $|E|=|\Omega|$ because sets of zero capacity are null. Hence $E=A\,\Omega^\star+x_0$ for some $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n$, and \eqref{eq:invariance} gives $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)\leq\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)$. By \eqref{eq:iso}, equality holds.

Conversely, suppose that equality holds in \eqref{eq:iso}, and let $u\geq0$ be a minimizer for $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_q=1$, given by Proposition \ref{prop:attain}. Then \eqref{eq:isochain} with $v=u$ is a chain of equalities, so that $|\Gamma_pL_u|=|L_u|$. By the equality case of \eqref{eq:BP}, $L_u$ is an origin-symmetric ellipsoid, and since $\Gamma_p$ commutes with linear maps and $\Gamma_pB^n=B^n$, we have $\Gamma_pL_u=L_u=A_0B^n$ for some $A_0\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$. Let $D=A_0^{-1}\Omega$ and $w=u\circ A_0\in W^{1,p}_0(D)$. By Lemma \ref{lem:Wulff}(iii), $\|w\|_q=1$ and $\|\nabla w\|_p^p=\int_\Omega h(\Gamma_pL_u,\nabla u)^p\,dx=\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)$, and $D^\star=\Omega^\star$. By the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} principle, $w^\star\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega^\star)$, $\|w^\star\|_q=1$ and $\|\nabla w^\star\|_p\leq\|\nabla w\|_p$; hence $w^\star$ is a nonnegative, radially nonincreasing minimizer for $\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)$, and $\|\nabla w^\star\|_p=\|\nabla w\|_p$. Let $R$ be the radius of $\Omega^\star$ and write $w^\star(x)=\varphi(|x|)$. By Lemma \ref{lem:radial}, $w^\star$ satisfies the non-degeneracy condition of the theorem of Brothers and Ziemer, since $\operatorname{ess\,sup}w=\operatorname{ess\,sup}w^\star$, and that theorem gives $w=w^\star(\cdot+y_0)$ a.e. for some $y_0\in\mathbb{R}^n$. With $A=A_0$ and $x_0=A_0y_0$, this reads
\[
u(x)=\varphi\big(|A^{-1}(x+x_0)|\big)\qquad\text{for a.e. }x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]
Let $E'=A\,\Omega^\star-x_0$, an open ellipsoid with $|E'|=|\Omega|$ and center $z=-x_0$. By Lemma \ref{lem:radial}, the right-hand side is positive and continuous in $E'\setminus\{z\}$. Being continuous, it is quasicontinuous there, so it coincides q.e. in $E'\setminus\{z\}$ with the quasicontinuous representative $\tilde u$ of $u$. On the other hand, $\tilde u=0$ q.e. in $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega$ by \eqref{eq:W0cap}. Therefore $C_p\big((E'\setminus\Omega)\setminus\{z\}\big)=0$. If $p\leq n$, points have zero Sobolev $p$-capacity. If $p>n$, $\tilde u$ is continuous and vanishes at every point of $\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\Omega$, while $\tilde u(z)=\lim_{r\to0^+}\varphi(r)>0$, so $z\in\Omega$. In both cases $C_p(E'\setminus\Omega)=0$; in particular $|E'\setminus\Omega|=0$, and since $|\Omega|=|E'|$, also $|\Omega\setminus E'|=0$. The open set $\Omega\setminus\overline{E'}$ is then null, hence empty, so $\Omega\subseteq\overline{E'}$ and, $\Omega$ being open, $\Omega\subseteq E'$. Thus $\Omega$ is an ellipsoid up to a set of zero Sobolev $p$-capacity.

title: Proof
body_md:
For $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$, a function $u$ belongs to $\mathcal{W}(K)$ if and only if $u\circ A^{-1}\in\mathcal{W}(AK)$, and $\mathcal{E}_p(u\circ A^{-1})=\mathcal{E}_p(u)$; hence $\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)=\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(AK)\leq\operatorname{cap}_p(AK)$, which is the upper bound.

For the lower bound, let $\varphi\in C^\infty_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\varphi\geq1$ on $K$, and let $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$ attain the minimum in \eqref{eq:HuangLi} for $f=\varphi$. Then $\varphi\circ A\geq1$ on $A^{-1}K$, so that
\[
\mathcal{E}_p(\varphi)^p\geq m_{n,p}^p\|\nabla(\varphi\circ A)\|_p^p\geq m_{n,p}^p\operatorname{cap}_p(A^{-1}K)\geq m_{n,p}^p\inf_{A'\in\mathrm{SL}(n)}\operatorname{cap}_p(A'K),
\]
and the lower bound follows by taking the infimum over $\varphi$.

For $p=2$, the remaining assertions are contained in Proposition \ref{prop:p2}.

Finally, if $K$ is contained in a hyperplane, which we may assume to be $e_n^\perp$, let $A_\varepsilon$ be the diagonal matrix with entries $\varepsilon^{1/(n-1)}$ in the first $n-1$ places and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ in the last one. Then $A_\varepsilon\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$, $A_\varepsilon K=\varepsilon^{1/(n-1)}K$, and $\operatorname{cap}_p(A_\varepsilon K)=\varepsilon^{(n-p)/(n-1)}\operatorname{cap}_p(K)\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$.

label: thm:Brasco
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Brasco}
Let $p>1$, $1<q<p^*$, and let $Q$ be an origin-symmetric convex body such that $Q^\circ$ is strictly convex and of class $C^1$. Then, for every open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of finite measure,
\[
T^{Q}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq T^{Q}_p(Q)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q),
\]
and equality holds if and only if $\Omega$ is a translate of a dilate of $Q$.

label: eq:KJchain
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $u$ be a minimizer for $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_q=1$ (Proposition \ref{prop:attain}), let $L_u$ be given by \eqref{eq:Lf} and set $Q=\Gamma_pL_u$. By Lemma \ref{lem:frozen},
\[
\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p=\int_\Omega h_Q(\nabla u)^p\,dx\geq\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega),
\]
and, since $\mathcal{E}_p(v)^p\leq\int_\Omega h_Q(\nabla v)^p\,dx$ for every $v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega)$, also $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)\geq T^{Q}_p(\Omega)$. By Lemma \ref{lem:admissible}, Theorem \ref{thm:Brasco} applies to $Q$, and by Lemma \ref{lem:Wulff}(i) and $|L_u|=\omega_n$ we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:KJchain}
T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq T^{Q}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq T^{Q}_p(Q)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(Q)=\Big(\frac{|\Gamma_pL_u|}{|L_u|}\Big)^{\theta}\,\kappa,
\end{equation}
where $\theta$ and $\kappa$ are as in \eqref{eq:Wulff}. By the $L_p$ Busemann--Petty centroid inequality \eqref{eq:BP}, the right-hand side is at least $\kappa$, which proves \eqref{eq:KJ}.

If equality holds in \eqref{eq:KJ}, then all the inequalities in \eqref{eq:KJchain} are equalities and $|\Gamma_pL_u|=|L_u|$, because $\theta>0$. By the equality case of \eqref{eq:BP}, $L_u$ is an origin-symmetric ellipsoid, and then $Q=\Gamma_pL_u=L_u$, since $\Gamma_p$ commutes with linear maps and $\Gamma_pB^n=B^n$. Equality in Theorem \ref{thm:Brasco} shows that $\Omega$ is a translate of a dilate of the ellipsoid $Q$, up to a set of zero Sobolev $p$-capacity. Conversely, if $\Omega$ is an ellipsoid up to a set of zero Sobolev $p$-capacity, Theorem \ref{thm:iso} and Corollary \ref{cor:SV} give $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)$ and $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)=T_p(\Omega^\star)$, and equality in \eqref{eq:KJ} follows from the invariance of the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:KJEuclid} under dilations.

label: rem:hierarchy
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:hierarchy}
As in \cite[Remark 1.2]{Brasco2014}, Theorem \ref{thm:KJ} and Corollary \ref{cor:SV} give, for $1<q<p^*$,
\[
\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\Big(\frac{T_p(\Omega^\star)}{T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)}\Big)^{(p-1)\sigma}\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)\geq\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star),
\]
where the first inequality is \eqref{eq:KJ} together with the dilation invariance of its right-hand side, and the second one is the affine Saint-Venant inequality. Thus the three classical inequalities of Saint-Venant, Faber--Krahn and Kohler-Jobin hold in affine form, with ellipsoids as the only extremals.

label: rem:p2KJ
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:p2KJ}
Since $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p\geq T_p$ and $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}\leq\Lambda_{p,q}$, inequality \eqref{eq:KJ} is not, in general, a strengthening of \eqref{eq:KJEuclid} in the sense in which \eqref{eq:iso} strengthens \eqref{eq:FK}. For $p=2$, Proposition \ref{prop:p2} shows that $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{2,q}(\Omega)$ and $T^{\mathcal{A}}_2(\Omega)$ are the minimum and the maximum of $\Lambda_{2,q}$ and $T_2$ over the images $A\Omega$, $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$. If $A_0\Omega$ minimizes $\Lambda_{2,q}$ among these images, then
\[
T^{\mathcal{A}}_2(\Omega)^{\sigma}\,\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{2,q}(\Omega)\geq T_2(A_0\Omega)^{\sigma}\,\Lambda_{2,q}(A_0\Omega),
\]
so that Theorem \ref{thm:KJ} for $p=2$, including its equality case, follows from \eqref{eq:KJEuclid} applied to $A_0\Omega$. For $p\neq2$ the anisotropic norm $h(\Gamma_pL_u,\cdot)$ is not ellipsoidal in general, and the proof above requires Brasco's anisotropic inequality together with the $L_p$ Busemann--Petty centroid inequality. Conversely, \eqref{eq:KJ} implies \eqref{eq:KJEuclid} for every $\Omega$ with $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)=T_p(\Omega)$, since then the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:KJEuclid} is at least that of \eqref{eq:KJ}.

Let $p\geq1$ and let $L$, $Q$ be star bodies. Then
\[
\widetilde{V}_{-p}(L,Q)\geq|L|^{\frac{n+p}{n}}|Q|^{-\frac pn}\Big(1+\frac{p}{8n}\,\eta^2\Big),\qquad\eta=\frac{|L\,\triangle\,(aQ)|}{|L|},\quad a=\Big(\frac{|L|}{|Q|}\Big)^{1/n}.
\]
head: environment

label: lem:symdiff
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:symdiff}
There exists $c_1=c_1(n)>0$ such that $|L\,\triangle\,Q|\geq c_1\,|L|\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L,Q)^n$ for all origin-symmetric convex bodies $L,Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $|L|=|Q|$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Both sides are invariant under simultaneous linear images of $L$ and $Q$, so by John's theorem we may assume $B^n\subseteq L\subseteq\sqrt nB^n$. Let $\varepsilon=|L\triangle Q|/|L|$ and let $\beta_n=|\{x\in B^n:\langle x,v\rangle>\frac12\}|$ for $v\in S^{n-1}$. Since $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L,Q)\leq\log n$, it suffices to consider $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0=\min\{\beta_n\omega_n^{-1}n^{-n/2},(20\sqrt n)^{-n}\}$.

First, $\frac12B^n\subseteq Q$. Otherwise there is $y\in\partial Q$ with $|y|<\frac12$; a supporting hyperplane of $Q$ at $y$ and the symmetry of $Q$ give $w\in S^{n-1}$ with $Q\subseteq\{|\langle x,w\rangle|\leq\frac12\}$, whence $|L\setminus Q|\geq|\{x\in B^n:\langle x,w\rangle>\frac12\}|=\beta_n\geq\varepsilon_0|L|$, a contradiction.

Next, let $x\in Q$ with $\|x\|_L=1+t$, $t>0$. For $b\in\frac12B^n$ and $s\in[0,1]$, the point $(1-s)x+sb$ belongs to $Q$, and since $\|b\|_L\leq|b|\leq\frac12$,
\[
\|(1-s)x+sb\|_L\geq(1-s)(1+t)-\tfrac s2>1\qquad\text{if }s<\tfrac{2t}{2t+3}.
\]
With $s_0=\frac{t}{2t+3}$, the ball $(1-s_0)x+\frac{s_0}2B^n$ is contained in $Q\setminus L$, and therefore $\omega_n(s_0/2)^n\leq\varepsilon|L|\leq\varepsilon\,\omega_nn^{n/2}$, that is, $s_0\leq2\sqrt n\,\varepsilon^{1/n}<\frac1{10}$. Hence $t\leq1$, $s_0\geq t/5$, and $t\leq10\sqrt n\,\varepsilon^{1/n}$; thus $Q\subseteq(1+10\sqrt n\,\varepsilon^{1/n})L$. The same argument with the roles of $L$ and $Q$ exchanged, now using $\frac14B^n\subseteq L$ and $\|b\|_Q\leq2|b|\leq\frac12$ for $b\in\frac14B^n$, gives $L\subseteq(1+20\sqrt n\,\varepsilon^{1/n})Q$. Therefore $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L,Q)\leq30\sqrt n\,\varepsilon^{1/n}$.

label: lem:Lipschitz
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Lipschitz}
Let $p\geq1$. There exists $C=C(n,p)$ such that $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pM,B^n)\leq C\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(M,B^n)$ for every origin-symmetric convex body $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $x\in S^{n-1}$ and let
\[
\Phi_x(y)=|\langle x,y\rangle|^p\,|y|^{1-p}+(p-1)|y|,\qquad y\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\qquad\Phi_x(0)=0.
\]
We claim that $\Phi_x$ is convex. The function $G(s,r)=r\,g(s/r)$ with $g(\tau)=|\tau|^p+p-1$ is the perspective of a convex function, hence convex on $\mathbb{R}\times(0,\infty)$, and $\partial_rG(s,r)=(p-1)\big(1-(|s|/r)^p\big)\geq0$ for $r\geq|s|$. Since $\Phi_x(y)=G(\langle x,y\rangle,|y|)$ and $|\langle x,y\rangle|\leq|y|$, for $y=\lambda y_1+(1-\lambda)y_2\neq0$ with $\lambda\in(0,1)$ we obtain
\[
\Phi_x(y)\leq G\big(\langle x,y\rangle,\lambda|y_1|+(1-\lambda)|y_2|\big)\leq\lambda\,\Phi_x(y_1)+(1-\lambda)\,\Phi_x(y_2),
\]
using that $G(\langle x,y\rangle,\cdot)$ is nondecreasing on $[|\langle x,y\rangle|,\infty)$ and the convexity of $G$ (the case where $y_1$ or $y_2$ vanishes is trivial). Hence $\Phi_x$ is the support function of an origin-symmetric convex body $Z_x$, and $|\langle x,v\rangle|^p=h_{Z_x}(v)-(p-1)$ for $v\in S^{n-1}$. Therefore, for every convex body $M$,
\[
\int_{S^{n-1}}|\langle x,v\rangle|^p\,dS_M(v)=n\,V(M[n-1],Z_x)-(p-1)\,n\,V(M[n-1],B^n).
\]

Let $\delta=\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(M,B^n)$. By the linear covariance of $\Pi^*_p$ and the invariance of $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}$, we may assume $B^n\subseteq M\subseteq e^\delta B^n$. Then $1\leq h_M\leq e^\delta$ on $S^{n-1}$, and by the monotonicity and homogeneity of mixed volumes, $V(B^n[n-1],Z)\leq V(M[n-1],Z)\leq e^{(n-1)\delta}V(B^n[n-1],Z)$ for $Z\in\{Z_x,B^n\}$. Since $nV(B^n[n-1],Z_x)=\int_{S^{n-1}}\Phi_x\,d\xi=n\omega_n(a_{n,p}+p-1)$ and $nV(B^n[n-1],B^n)=n\omega_n$, we get
\[
n\omega_n\big(a_{n,p}-(p-1)(e^{(n-1)\delta}-1)\big)\leq\int_{S^{n-1}}|\langle x,v\rangle|^p\,dS_M(v)\leq n\omega_n\big(a_{n,p}+(a_{n,p}+p-1)(e^{(n-1)\delta}-1)\big).
\]
Combining this with $e^{-(p-1)\delta}\leq h_M^{1-p}\leq1$ and \eqref{eq:GammaPi}, and writing $\beta=(p-1)/a_{n,p}$, we obtain for every $x\in S^{n-1}$
\[
e^{-(p-1)\delta}\big(1-\beta\,(e^{(n-1)\delta}-1)\big)\leq h(\Pi_pM,x)^p\leq1+(1+\beta)(e^{(n-1)\delta}-1).
\]
Let $\delta_0=\delta_0(n,p)>0$ be such that $\beta\,(e^{(n-1)\delta_0}-1)\leq\frac12$. If $\delta\leq\delta_0$, then, using $1-\tau\geq e^{-2\tau}$ for $\tau\in[0,\frac12]$ and $e^{(n-1)\delta}-1\leq(n-1)e^{(n-1)\delta_0}\delta$, both bounds are of the form $e^{\pm C_1\delta}$ with $C_1=C_1(n,p)$. Hence $e^{-C_1\delta/p}B^n\subseteq\Pi_pM\subseteq e^{C_1\delta/p}B^n$, the same inclusions hold for $\Pi^*_pM$, and $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pM,B^n)\leq2C_1\delta/p$. If $\delta>\delta_0$, then $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pM,B^n)\leq\frac12\log n\leq\frac{\log n}{2\delta_0}\,\delta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $L$ be an origin-symmetric convex body, let $M=\Gamma_pL$ and $Q=\Pi^*_pM$, both origin-symmetric convex bodies, and set
\[
\delta=\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L,B^n),\qquad\delta_1=\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(M,B^n),\qquad\delta_2=\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L,Q),\qquad N=840(n+p).
\]
By Lemma \ref{lem:classreduction} with this $M$, $|M|=V_p(M,M)=\frac{\omega_n}{|L|}\widetilde{V}_{-p}(L,Q)$. By Lemma \ref{lem:Nguyen} and Theorem \ref{thm:Boroczky},
\[
|M|\geq\omega_n\,|L|^{\frac pn}|Q|^{-\frac pn}\Big(1+\frac{p}{8n}\eta^2\Big)\geq|L|^{\frac pn}|M|^{\frac{n-p}{n}}\big(1-\gamma_0\delta_1^N\big)^{-\frac pn}\Big(1+\frac{p}{8n}\eta^2\Big),
\]
with $\eta=|L\triangle(aQ)|/|L|$ and $a=(|L|/|Q|)^{1/n}$. Hence
\[
\frac{|M|}{|L|}\geq\big(1-\gamma_0\delta_1^N\big)^{-1}\Big(1+\frac{p}{8n}\eta^2\Big)^{\frac np}\geq\big(1+\gamma_0\delta_1^N\big)\big(1+c_2\eta^2\big)\geq1+\gamma_0\delta_1^N+c_2\eta^2,
\]
where $c_2=c_2(n,p)>0$; here we used $\eta\leq2$ and $(1+\tau)^{n/p}\geq1+\frac np\frac{\tau}{1+\tau}$ for $\tau\geq0$. Since $|aQ|=|L|$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L,aQ)=\delta_2$, Lemma \ref{lem:symdiff} gives $\eta\geq c_1\delta_2^n$. By Lemma \ref{lem:Lipschitz} and the triangle inequality, $\delta\leq\delta_2+\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(Q,B^n)\leq\delta_2+C\delta_1$. Since $\delta_2\leq\log n$ and $N\geq2n$, we have $\delta_2^{2n}\geq(\log n)^{2n-N}\delta_2^N$, and therefore
\[
\frac{|\Gamma_pL|}{|L|}-1\geq\gamma_0\delta_1^N+c_2c_1^2\delta_2^{2n}\geq c_3\big(\delta_1^N+\delta_2^N\big)\geq c_3\,2^{1-N}(\delta_1+\delta_2)^N\geq\gamma\,\delta^N,
\]
with $c_3$ and $\gamma$ depending only on $n$ and $p$.
head: environment

label: prop:bodystab
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:bodystab}
Let $\gamma=\gamma(n,p)$ be the constant of Theorem \ref{thm:BPstab}, let $N=840(n+p)$, and let $\theta$ and $\kappa$ be as in \eqref{eq:Wulff}.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $p>1$, $1\leq q<p^*$ and $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a bounded open set, then, for every minimizer $u$ for $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$,
\[
\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\big(1+\gamma\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)^N\big)^{\frac pn}\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star).
\]
\item If $1<p<n$ and $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact set with $|K|>0$, then, for every minimizer $u$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:potential},
\[
\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)\geq\big(1+\gamma\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)^N\big)^{\frac pn}\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star).
\]
\item If $p>1$, $1<q<p^*$ and $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a bounded open set, then, for every minimizer $u$ for $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$,
\[
T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\big(1+\gamma\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)^N\big)^{\theta}\,\kappa.
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In each case $L_u$ is a dilate of the origin-symmetric convex body $\Pi^*_pu$, and the Banach--Mazur distance is invariant under dilations, so that Theorem \ref{thm:BPstab} gives
\[
\frac{|\Gamma_pL_u|}{|L_u|}\geq1+\gamma\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)^N,
\]
and it remains to bound the three quantities from below by the corresponding powers of this ratio times the Euclidean values. For (i), by homogeneity we may assume $\|u\|_q=1$; then $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p$, and \eqref{eq:isochain} with $v=u$ gives the power $p/n$. For (ii), $\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)=\mathcal{E}_p(u)^p$, and \eqref{eq:capchain} gives the power $p/n$. For (iii), by homogeneity we may assume $\|u\|_q=1$, and then \eqref{eq:KJchain} gives the power $\theta$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We begin with (ii). Let $\varepsilon\geq0$ be defined by $\operatorname{cap}^{\mathcal{A}}_p(K)=(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star)$. Since $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(K)\leq2$, we may assume that $\varepsilon\leq1$. For every $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$ we have $|AK|=|K|$ and $\mathcal{F}(AK)\geq\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(K)$.

If $p=2$, Theorem \ref{thm:DPMM} gives $\operatorname{cap}_2(AK)\geq\big(1+c_{\mathrm{cap}}\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(K)^2\big)\operatorname{cap}_2(K^\star)$ for every $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$, and taking the infimum over $A$, Proposition \ref{prop:compare} proves the claim with $c=c_{\mathrm{cap}}$.

Let $p\neq2$, let $u$ be a minimizer given by Theorem \ref{thm:potential}, and set $\delta=\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)$, $\eta=\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Gamma_pL_u,B^n)$ and $N=840(n+p)$. By Proposition \ref{prop:bodystab}(ii), $(1+\gamma\delta^N)^{p/n}\leq1+\varepsilon$, and since $(1+\varepsilon)^{n/p}-1\leq(2^{n/p}-1)\varepsilon$ for $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, we get $\delta\leq C_1\varepsilon^{1/N}$. If $E'$ is an origin-symmetric ellipsoid with $E'\subseteq L_u\subseteq e^{\delta}E'$, then \eqref{eq:GammaPi} gives $e^{-\delta n/p}\,\Gamma_pE'\subseteq\Gamma_pL_u\subseteq e^{\delta(n+p)/p}\,\Gamma_pE'$, and $\Gamma_pE'$ is an ellipsoid; hence $\eta\leq\frac{2n+p}{p}\delta\leq C_2\varepsilon^{1/N}$. Let $E=tA_0B^n$, with $t>0$ and $A_0\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$, be an origin-symmetric ellipsoid with $E\subseteq\Gamma_pL_u\subseteq e^{\eta}E$. Then $t^n=|E|/\omega_n\geq e^{-n\eta}|\Gamma_pL_u|/\omega_n\geq e^{-n\eta}$ by the $L_p$ Busemann--Petty centroid inequality. As $H_u=h(\Gamma_pL_u,\cdot)\geq h_E$, Lemma \ref{lem:Wulff}(iii) and Theorem \ref{thm:DPMM} give
\begin{align*}
(1+\varepsilon)\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star)&=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}H_u(\nabla u)^p\,dx\geq\operatorname{cap}^{E}_p(K)=t^p\operatorname{cap}_p(A_0^{-1}K)\\
&\geq e^{-p\eta}\big(1+c_{\mathrm{cap}}\,\mathcal{F}(A_0^{-1}K)^2\big)\operatorname{cap}_p(K^\star).
\end{align*}
Consequently $c_{\mathrm{cap}}\,\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(K)^2\leq c_{\mathrm{cap}}\,\mathcal{F}(A_0^{-1}K)^2\leq(1+\varepsilon)e^{pC_2\varepsilon^{1/N}}-1\leq C_3\varepsilon^{1/N}$, which is the claim with $\beta=2N$. The constants $C_1,C_2,C_3$ depend only on $n$ and $p$.

We turn to (i). Let $\varepsilon\geq0$ be defined by $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)=(1+\varepsilon)\Lambda_{p,q}(\Omega^\star)$. If $p=2$, Proposition \ref{prop:p2} gives $A\in\mathrm{SL}(n)$ with $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{2,q}(\Omega)=\Lambda_{2,q}(A\Omega)$; since $|A\Omega|=|\Omega|$ and $\mathcal{F}(A\Omega)\geq\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(\Omega)$, \eqref{eq:quantFK} gives the claim with $\beta=2$. If $p\neq2$, the argument above applies verbatim, with $\Lambda_{p,q}$ in place of $\operatorname{cap}_p$, a minimizer $u$ for $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_q=1$ in place of the potential, Proposition \ref{prop:bodystab}(i) in place of Proposition \ref{prop:bodystab}(ii), the identity $\Lambda^{E}_{p,q}(\Omega)=t^p\Lambda_{p,q}(A_0^{-1}\Omega)$ given by Lemma \ref{lem:Wulff}(iii) in place of its capacitary form, and \eqref{eq:quantFK} in place of Theorem \ref{thm:DPMM}. The case $q=1$ gives the bound for $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p$.

title: Proof
body_md:
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{prop:bodystab}(iii), we may assume $u\geq0$ and $\|u\|_q=1$. Let $Q=\Gamma_pL_u$, and let $E=AB^n$, with $\det A>0$, be an origin-symmetric ellipsoid such that $E\subseteq Q\subseteq e^{\eta}E$. Since $h_E\leq h_Q\leq e^{\eta}h_E$, we have $\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq\Lambda^{E}_{p,q}(\Omega)$ and $\Lambda^{Q}_{p,1}(\Omega)\leq e^{p\eta}\Lambda^{E}_{p,1}(\Omega)$, that is, $T^{Q}_p(\Omega)\geq e^{-p\eta/(p-1)}T^{E}_p(\Omega)$. Combining the first inequality in \eqref{eq:KJchain} with Lemma \ref{lem:Wulff}(iii) and the identity $(p-1)\sigma+1-\frac pq=\theta$, we obtain
\[
(1+\varepsilon)\,\kappa\geq T^{Q}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{Q}_{p,q}(\Omega)\geq e^{-p\sigma\eta}\,(\det A)^{\theta}\,T_p(A^{-1}\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda_{p,q}(A^{-1}\Omega).
\]
Since $Q\subseteq e^{\eta}E$ and $|Q|\geq|L_u|=\omega_n$ by \eqref{eq:BP}, we have $\det A=|E|/\omega_n\geq e^{-n\eta}$, and \eqref{eq:reduction} follows. If $E'\subseteq L_u\subseteq e^{s}E'$ for an origin-symmetric ellipsoid $E'$, then \eqref{eq:GammaPi} gives $e^{-sn/p}\,\Gamma_pE'\subseteq\Gamma_pL_u\subseteq e^{s(n+p)/p}\,\Gamma_pE'$, and $\Gamma_pE'$ is an ellipsoid; hence $\eta\leq\frac{2n+p}{p}\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(L_u,B^n)=\frac{2n+p}{p}\,\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)$. For $\varepsilon\leq1$, Proposition \ref{prop:bodystab}(iii) gives $\delta_{\mathrm{BM}}(\Pi^*_pu,B^n)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/(840(n+p))}$, and the bound on the left-hand side of \eqref{eq:reduction} follows. Finally, for $p=2$ the body $\Pi^*_2u$ is an ellipsoid, so $L_u$ is an origin-symmetric ellipsoid of volume $\omega_n$ and $Q=\Gamma_2L_u=L_u$; we may take $E=Q$, so that $\eta=0$ and $\det A=1$.

label: rem:dust
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:dust}
Let $V>0$, let $W$ be a cube with $|W|=2^{n+1}V/\omega_n$ at distance $R$ from $B^n$, and for small $r>0$ let $D_r\subseteq W$ be the union of $N_r=\lfloor V/(\omega_nr^n)\rfloor$ pairwise disjoint balls of radius $r$, for instance centered at points of $2r\mathbb{Z}^n$. Let $\Omega_r=B^n\cup D_r$. For every origin-symmetric convex body $Q$, the functional $T^{Q}_p$ is subadditive on disjoint unions of open sets, as follows from H\"older's inequality applied to $v=v_1+v_2$ with $v_i\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega_i)$. By \eqref{eq:envelope}, $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)$ is the supremum of $T^{\Gamma_pL}_p(\Omega)$ over star bodies $L$ with $|L|=\omega_n$, and $T^{\Gamma_pL}_p(B_r)\leq T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(B_r)=T_p(B_r)=r^{n+p'}\,T_p(B^n)$ by Corollary \ref{cor:SV}. Hence
\[
T_p(B^n)\leq T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega_r)\leq T_p(B^n)+N_r\,T_p(B_r)\leq\Big(1+\frac{V}{\omega_n}\,r^{p'}\Big)\,T_p(B^n),
\]
while $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega_r)\leq\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(B^n)=\Lambda_{p,q}(B^n)$. Therefore the deficit in \eqref{eq:KJ} for $\Omega_r$ tends to $0$ as $r\to0$, and the same argument applies to \eqref{eq:KJEuclid}. On the other hand, an ellipsoid $E$ with $|E\triangle\Omega_r|<\frac14\min\{\omega_n,V\}$ contains subsets of $B^n$ and of $D_r$ of volume at least $\frac14\min\{\omega_n,V\}$ for $r$ small, and hence their convex hull, whose volume tends to infinity with $R$ by the Brunn--Minkowski inequality. Choosing $R$ large, depending only on $n$ and $V$, we obtain $|E\triangle\Omega_r|\geq\frac14\min\{\omega_n,V\}$ for every ellipsoid $E$ and every small $r$. Thus, since $|\Omega_r|\leq\omega_n+V$, we have $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(\Omega_r)\geq\min\{\omega_n,V\}/\big(4(\omega_n+V)\big)$ for all small $r$, while the deficit in \eqref{eq:KJ} tends to $0$: for general open sets, the deficit does not control the affine Fraenkel asymmetry.

label: eq:sandwich
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\kappa$ be as in \eqref{eq:Wulff} and write $P(\Omega)=T^{\mathcal{A}}_p(\Omega)^{(p-1)\sigma}\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}(\Omega)$. By \eqref{eq:invariance}, $P$ is invariant under affine maps with positive determinant, and so is the conclusion of (iii). Moreover, $T^{\mathcal{A}}_p$ is nondecreasing and $\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}$ is nonincreasing with respect to inclusion. Hence, if $(1-\tau)\Omega'\subseteq\Omega\subseteq(1+\tau)\Omega'$ for an open set $\Omega'$ and $\tau\in(0,1)$, then, since $(p-1)\sigma(n+p')=p+\frac{np}{q}-n>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:sandwich}
P(\Omega)\geq T^{\mathcal{A}}_p\big((1-\tau)\Omega'\big)^{(p-1)\sigma}\,\Lambda^{\mathcal{A}}_{p,q}\big((1+\tau)\Omega'\big)=\Big(\frac{1-\tau}{1+\tau}\Big)^{p+\frac{np}{q}-n}P(\Omega').
\end{equation}

Suppose that (iii) fails for some $\eta>0$. Then there are bounded open convex sets $\Omega_k$ with $P(\Omega_k)\leq(1+\frac1k)\kappa$ for which no ellipsoid has the stated property. By John's theorem \cite{John1948} and the affine invariance, we may assume $B^n\subseteq\overline{\Omega_k}\subseteq nB^n$. By the Blaschke selection theorem, a subsequence of $(\overline{\Omega_k})$ converges in the Hausdorff metric to a convex body $K_\infty$ with $B^n\subseteq K_\infty\subseteq nB^n$. Since all these bodies contain $B^n$, their radial functions converge uniformly, so that $(1-\tau_k)\Omega_\infty\subseteq\Omega_k\subseteq(1+\tau_k)\Omega_\infty$, where $\Omega_\infty=\operatorname{int}K_\infty$ and $\tau_k\to0$. By \eqref{eq:sandwich}, $P(\Omega_\infty)\leq\kappa$, so equality holds in \eqref{eq:KJ} for $\Omega_\infty$, and by Theorem \ref{thm:KJ} there is an open ellipsoid $E$ with $\Omega_\infty\subseteq E$ and $C_p(E\setminus\Omega_\infty)=0$. Since sets of zero Sobolev $p$-capacity have measure zero, $E\setminus\Omega_\infty$ has empty interior, so $\Omega_\infty$ is dense in $E$. Hence, $K_\infty\supseteq E$ and $\Omega_\infty=\operatorname{int}K_\infty\supseteq E$; hence $\Omega_\infty=E$. Let $z$ be the center of $E$. Since $B^n\subseteq E\subseteq nB^n$ and $E$ is symmetric about $z$, we have $B^n\subseteq E-z$ and $|z|\leq n$. Therefore the ellipsoid $E_k=(1-\tau_k)E$, whose center is $z_k=(1-\tau_k)z$, satisfies
\[
E_k\subseteq\Omega_k\subseteq(1+\tau_k)E\subseteq z_k+\frac{1+(2n+1)\tau_k}{1-\tau_k}\,(E_k-z_k),
\]
which contradicts the choice of $\Omega_k$ for $k$ large.

Finally, let $E$ and $z$ be as in the conclusion of (iii). Since $|E|\leq|\Omega|\leq e^{n\eta}|E|$, the ellipsoid $E_0=z+s(E-z)$ with $s=(|\Omega|/|E|)^{1/n}\in[1,e^{\eta}]$ satisfies $|E_0|=|\Omega|$ and $E\subseteq E_0\subseteq z+e^{\eta}(E-z)$. As $\Omega$ lies between the same two sets, $|\Omega\triangle E_0|\leq\big|\big(z+e^{\eta}(E-z)\big)\setminus E\big|=(e^{n\eta}-1)|E|\leq(e^{n\eta}-1)|\Omega|$, and therefore $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{aff}}(\Omega)\leq e^{n\eta}-1$.
